title: Microsoft Purview: Data Security Triage Agent summaries for DLP alerts in Microsoft Defender XDR
summary: The briefing's controls, licensing and conditional default state are supported by Microsoft's documentation and notice. Minor corrections should preserve the notice's planned preview wording, acknowledge conflicting identity documentation and identify a checklist control missing from the table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to make Data Security Triage Agent summaries and categorizations available in DLP alerts in Defender XDR.
claims.quote: Data Security Triage Agent summaries and categorizations for DLP alerts will be made available in DLP Alerts in Microsoft Defender XDR.

claims.claim: The change does not alter existing DLP policies or enforcement.

claims.claim: Custom instructions and pausing or deactivating the agent remain in Purview.

claims.claim: Agent usage monitoring remains in Purview.

claims.claim: The notice identifies security analysts, admins and agent-using organisations as affected.
claims.quote:
Security analysts and admins triaging DLP alerts in Microsoft Defender XDR
- Organizations using Microsoft Purview Data Security Triage Agent

claims.claim: The Defender XDR display change is on when the agent is deployed.
claims.quote: DLP alerts in Defender XDR will display AI-generated summaries and categorizations when the Agent is deployed.

claims.quote:
Will Microsoft Security Copilot agents be automatically enabled?

No, a customer's organization is required to set up and deploy agents in the relevant standalone or embedded experiences.

claims.claim: There can be only one instance of this agent per tenant regardless of the deployment portal.
claims.quote: There can be only one instance of each agent in a tenant, regardless of the portal in which it was deployed.

claims.claim: Removal is also a Purview-only operation.
claims.quote: Agent can only be removed from the Microsoft Purview portal even if it was deployed from the Defender XDR portal.

claims.quote: Any admin or analyst for a tenant (with no agent deployed) sees a banner or card on alerts page for Triage agent setup.

claims.quote: Click on "Get started" to start the agent with default settings.

claims.quote:
select Agents.

select Agents.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or other API for deploying or configuring this agent is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Data Security Triage Agent DLP API PowerShell Graph deploy configure deactivate usage monitoring; PowerShell 'triage' 'agent' 'DLP'; Graph 'triage' 'agent' 'Purview'. Opened DLP agent get-started and agents overview; no matching operation.

claims.quote: select Agents. ... Select Explore agents. ... Select Go to agent for the agent you want to deactivate. ... select the ellipses (three dots) that are located next to the Edit agent button. ... Select Deactivate agent.

claims.claim: Deactivation stops alert triage.
claims.quote: Deactivating the agent stops the agent from triaging alerts.

claims.claim: Deactivation does not remove the agent.
claims.quote: It doesn't remove the agent and it doesn't reset the Select alert timeframe reference point in time.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or other API for deactivating this agent is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview Data Security Triage Agent DLP API PowerShell Graph deploy configure deactivate usage monitoring'; PowerShell and Graph searches for triage agent DLP/Purview. Opened DLP agent get-started and agents overview; only portal deactivation was documented.

claims.claim: Purview's Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users reaches role group membership selection.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... select a Microsoft Purview role group you want to add users to. Select Edit on the control bar. ... On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The Exchange PowerShell cmdlet is also used in Security & Compliance PowerShell for a Purview role group.
claims.quote: You can add a mail-enabled security group as a member of the eDiscovery Managers subgroup in the eDiscovery Manager role group by using the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends creating a separate Microsoft Entra agent identity.
claims.quote: Create and use agent identity (recommended): Create a separate Microsoft Entra agent identity for the agent. Associate all agent activities with this agent identity.
claims.fix: Add to the identity discussion: 'The get-started and overview pages recommend an agent identity, although the separate preview page still describes the DLP agent as running under the administrator who enabled it.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/copilot-in-purview-agents, whose DLP Identity row says 'Runs as the administrator who turned on the agent.'

claims.claim: The one-click default identity is Create and use agent identity.
claims.quote:
The default settings for 'One-Click' setup are:
- Identity: Create and use agent identity

claims.claim: The alternative uses the setup user's identity and associates all agent activities with that identity.
claims.quote: Assign and use my identity: Set up the agent by using the identity of the user or admin who sets up the agent. Associate all activities with the user's identity.

claims.claim: The agent identity is assigned Data classification content downloader for the endpoint scenario.
claims.quote: These roles are assigned to the Triage agent in DLP when agent identity is used: ... Data classification content downloader (needed for endpoint scenario)

claims.quote: Agents aren't administrative unit aware.

claims.claim: An agent running in an administrative-unit-restricted admin's context sees only alerts from policies scoped to that admin unit.
claims.quote: But if the agent runs in the context of an administrative-unit restricted admin, and there are policies that are administrative-unit scoped to that admin, the agent only sees alerts from the policies that scoped to the admin unit.

claims.quote: Choose to Run automatically based on a set schedule. ... Microsoft sets the schedule and it isn't configurable by organizations.

claims.quote: select whether the agent runs automatically based on a set schedule or the Agent runs manually on one alert at a time

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions

claims.claim: The tenant must be onboarded to Security Copilot.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview plug-in must be enabled in Security Copilot.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The agent supports active-mode DLP policies rather than policies in simulation mode.
claims.quote: The Triage agent in DLP only supports alerts from policies that are in active mode. It doesn't triage alerts from DLP policies that are running in simulation mode.

claims.claim: Supported DLP locations are Exchange, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and devices.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Purview Triage Agent in DLP triages alerts from policies that are scoped to Exchange, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and devices (Endpoint) locations, only.

claims.claim: Triaging device alerts requires evidence collection for file activities on devices.
claims.quote: If you want to triage alerts from devices, Evidence collection for file activities on devices must be enabled.

claims.claim: The agent starts running within 30 to 60 minutes after setup.
claims.quote: After setup is complete, the agent starts running within 30–60 minutes and begins triaging DLP alerts.

claims.where: Scope: default policy scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The default agent policy scope includes all DLP policies in scope for triage.
claims.quote: Policy scope: All policies in scope for triage.

claims.where: Scope: default timeframe; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The default alert timeframe is the past 30 days.
claims.quote: Alert timeframe: Triage alerts from the last 30 days

claims.claim: Teams admin settings must allow the Data Security Triage Agent app to deliver remediation messages.
claims.quote: The Data Security Triage Agent app must not be blocked for users who should receive remediation messages.

claims.claim: Learn says to wait 30 minutes after agent-identity setup before initiating a manual run.
claims.quote: Wait for 30-min post setting the agent with agent identity for the roles based access to get reflected before initiating any manual run on an alert.

claims.claim: Learn says to allow up to two hours for initial in-scope alert triage.
claims.quote: Allow up to 2 hours for the agent to complete triaging in-scope alerts and enabled manual runs after this initial setup.

claims.claim: MC1255406 advises updating security operations documentation and familiarising teams with deployment and management locations.
claims.quote: Update internal security operations documentation to reflect the new triage experience.- Familiarize security teams with where Agent deployment can occur (Defender XDR) and where ongoing management is performed (Purview).

claims.claim: Provisioned and overage SCUs can be changed in the Azure and Security Copilot portals.
claims.quote: You can update provisioned security compute units and overage units in the Azure portal and the Security Copilot portal.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: Every control the checklist tells the reader to check is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Check that the tenant is onboarded to Security Copilot and has SCUs provisioned or the E5/E7 inclusion capacity ... Table: agent configuration; deactivation; role group membership; agent SCU consumption monitoring.
